gloss: rise, dawn, shine forth (of the sun, light); the sunrise, east; native
summary: זָרַח is what the sun does at dawn: it rises and its light breaks out on the land (Gen 32:32; Ecc 1:5), and so of light rising in darkness, of Yahweh rising upon his people and of “the sun of righteousness” that “will rise” with healing (Deu 33:2; Isa 60:1–2; Mal 3:20); once it is leprosy breaking out on Uzziah’s forehead (2Ch 26:19). מִזְרָח is the place of the sun’s rising, the east, and with the sun’s setting it spans the whole earth (Psa 50:1; 113:3). אֶזְרָח is the native, the Israelite born in the land, always set beside the sojourner who lives among Israel (Exo 12:48–49; Lev 23:42); how it comes from “rise” is not clear. Aramaic has the same root as דְּנַח “shine, rise” and מַדְנְחָא “east”, the Peshitta’s words for the dawning light of Mat 4:16 and the east of Mat 2:1.

words.gloss: sunrise, the place of the sun’s rising; east
words.summary: The place where the sun rises, and so the east: a side of the tabernacle court or a camp, the eastern bounds of the tribes, and, set against the sun’s setting, the far ends of the earth.

senses.definition: With שֶׁמֶשׁ, the rising of the sun, as the place it comes up: “from the rising of the sun to its going in” spans the earth from one side to the other.

evidence.note: God “has called the earth from the rising of the sun (מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁמֶשׁ) to its going in (מְבֹאוֹ)”.
“From the rising of the sun to its going in, the name of Yahweh is to be praised.”
“From the rising of the sun to its going in my name will be great among the nations.”
“That they may know from the rising of the sun and from the west (מִמַּעֲרָבָה) that there is none beside me.”
They will fear the name of Yahweh from the west and his glory from the rising of the sun.
Iye-abarim, before Moab, “toward the rising of the sun”.
Three cities beyond the Jordan “toward the rising of the sun”.
Shiloh lies “toward the rising of the sun” of the road from Bethel to Shechem.

senses.definition: The direction of sunrise, without the sun named: the east side of the court and of the camp, the eastern bounds of land and city, one of the four winds.

evidence.note: The breadth of the court “on the side קֵדְמָה מִזְרָחָה”, eastward toward the sunrise: 50 cubits.
Judah’s standard camps “eastward, toward the sunrise”, before the tent of meeting.
Moses, Aaron and his sons camp before the tabernacle toward the east, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The gatekeepers were on the four winds: מִזְרָח, west, north and south.
Of the twelve oxen under the sea, three faced north, three west, three south and three east.
Reuben and Gad: “our inheritance has come to us beyond the Jordan eastward”.
Gilgal, at the east border of Jericho.

senses.gloss: the east, as the far lands
senses.definition: The east as one end of the earth, from which Yahweh calls a conqueror and gathers his scattered people, and which stands with the west for the widest distance there is.

evidence.note: “From the east I will bring your seed, and from the west I will gather you.”
The redeemed gathered “from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the sea”.
“I will save my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the going in of the sun.”
“As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.”
Who stirred up one from the east, whom righteousness calls to its foot?
One raised from the north, “from the rising of the sun”, who will call on Yahweh’s name.
“Calling a bird of prey from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country.”
They wander from sea to sea and from the north to the east seeking the word of Yahweh, and will not find it.
The little horn grows toward the south, toward the east and toward the beauty.
The Mount of Olives splits in two “toward the east and toward the west”.

evidence.locator: Psa.50.1, Psa.113.3, Mal.1.11, Isa.43.5, מִזְרָח → ἀνατολή; ἀνατολή renders מִזְרָח ×35

evidence.note: “Many will come from the east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens”, as Isa 43:5 and Psa 107:3 gather Israel from east and west.
“They will come from east and west, and from north and south.”
Wise men came from the east to Jerusalem.
An angel ascending “from the rising of the sun”.
The kings “from the rising of the sun”.
Three gates on the east of the city.

opposites.note: The sun’s “going in”, its setting: the west, at the other end of the earth.
“West”, set against it as the farthest distance.
“Sea”, Israel’s word for west, against it in the four quarters and the two halves of the Mount of Olives.

parallels.note: “Eastward, toward the front”: Israel’s other word for east, joined with it.

phrases.gloss: from the rising of the sun to its going in: the whole earth

words.gloss: rise, dawn; shine forth; break out
words.summary: Used of the sun coming up and its light breaking on the land, and from there of light, glory and Yahweh himself rising upon his people. Two of the tokens counted under its key are the name Zerah pointed in pause (Gen 38:30; 1Ch 2:4).

stems.gloss: rise, dawn; shine forth; break out

senses.definition: The sun coming up at dawn and its light falling on someone or something: the time a day’s work or a thief’s deed is reckoned from, and the counterpart of the sun’s going in.

evidence.note: “The sun rises (זָרַח) and the sun goes in (בָּא), and panting to its place, it rises (זוֹרֵחַ) there.”
“The sun rose on him as he passed Penuel”, after the night of wrestling.
A thief struck by night brings no bloodguilt, but “if the sun has risen on him”, there is bloodguilt.
“In the morning, as the sun rises, rise early and rush on the city.”
The just ruler is “like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds”.
The sun rose on the water, and Moab saw it red as blood.
When the sun rose, God appointed a hot east wind.
Nineveh’s officers are like locusts that settle on the walls in the cold and fly away when the sun rises.
“The sun rises; they withdraw and lie down in their dens.”
God “speaks to the sun and it does not rise”.

senses.gloss: rise, shine forth, of light, glory and Yahweh
senses.definition: Light rising out of darkness, and Yahweh and his glory rising upon his people like the dawn: coming into view and lighting them.

evidence.note: “Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of Yahweh has risen (זָרָח) upon you.”
Darkness covers the earth, “but upon you Yahweh will rise, and his glory will be seen upon you”.
“Yahweh came from Sinai and rose from Seir to them; he shone forth (הוֹפִיעַ) from Mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of holy ones.”
“For you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its wings.”
If you satisfy the afflicted soul, “your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom be as noon”.
“Light rises in the darkness for the upright.”

senses.definition: Leprosy appearing suddenly on the skin, as light breaks out at dawn.

evidence.note: While Uzziah raged at the priests with the censer in his hand, “the leprosy rose (זָרְחָה) on his forehead”.

greek.gloss: rise, spring up (of the sun, light)

evidence.locator: Gen.32.32, Ecc.1.5, Isa.60.1, Mal.3.20, זָרַח → ἀνατέλλω; ἀνατέλλω renders זָרַח ×13

evidence.note: “To those sitting in the region and shadow of death light has risen (ἀνέτειλεν)”: Isa 9:1, which has נָגַהּ, read in the language of Isa 58:10 and 60:1.
The Father “makes his sun rise on the evil and the good”.
The women came to the tomb “when the sun had risen”.
“The sun rises with burning heat and withers the grass.”
Until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
“Our Lord has risen (ἀνατέταλκεν) out of Judah.”
The dawn from on high visits us “to shine upon (ἐπιφᾶναι) those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death”.
“The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared (ἐπεφάνη) to all men.”

parallels.note: “Shine forth”: Yahweh rose from Seir and shone forth from Paran.
“Be seen”: Yahweh rises upon Zion and his glory is seen upon her.
“Shine” and “light”: “Arise, shine (אוֹרִי), for your light has come.”

words.gloss: native, one born in the land
words.summary: The Israelite born in the land, named almost always beside the sojourner (גֵּר) to say that one law binds both; once a tree growing in its own soil. How it comes from “rise” is not clear: it may be one who has sprung up from the soil, as the tree of Psa 37:35, but scripture does not say so, and no cognate shares the sense.

senses.definition: One born in Israel’s land and people, as against the sojourner who has come to live among them; the law sets the two side by side and holds them to one statute.

evidence.note: A sojourner who would keep the Passover is to be circumcised, and “he will be like the native of the land (כְּאֶזְרַח הָאָרֶץ)”.
“One law shall be for the native and for the sojourner who sojourns among you.”
“The sojourner who sojourns with you shall be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.”
“The native among the sons of Israel and the sojourner among them: one law for you.”
“All the native in Israel shall dwell in booths”, that their generations may know Yahweh made Israel dwell in booths when he brought them out of Egypt (Lev 23:43).
Whoever eats leaven is cut off, “whether a sojourner or a native of the land”.
The Day of Coverings binds the native and the sojourner.
The blasphemer of the Name dies, “as the sojourner, so the native”.
“One judgment for you: as the sojourner, so the native.”
One statute for the Passover, for the sojourner and the native of the land.
All Israel stood at Ebal and Gerizim, “as the sojourner, so the native”.
In the land divided in the coming age, sojourners who have had sons among Israel “shall be to you as the native among the sons of Israel” and inherit among the tribes.

senses.definition: A tree growing where it sprang up, flourishing and spreading in its own ground.

evidence.note: “I have seen the wicked, ruthless, spreading himself like a green native (כְּאֶזְרָח רַעֲנָן)”; yet “he passed away, and behold, he was not” (Psa 37:36).

opposites.note: “Sojourner”, the man of another people living among Israel: named against it in nearly every use.

phrases.gloss: as the sojourner, so the native: the one and the other alike

words.summary: Used once, of Zion lit by Yahweh’s glory: the brightness that rises on her draws the nations.

senses.definition: The light that rises on Zion when Yahweh’s glory rises on her (Isa 60:1–2).

evidence.note: “Nations will walk to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising (נֹגַהּ זַרְחֵךְ).”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s verb for the sun rising and light dawning, the Aramaic form of זָרַח with d for z and n for r; it renders both ἀνατέλλω and λάμπω.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “when the sun rose (דְּנַח), it was scorched”.
Peshitta: “as the sun rose” the women came to the tomb.
Peshitta: the sun rises with its heat and withers the grass.
Peshitta: “when you see a cloud rising (דָּדְנְחָא) from the west”.

senses.gloss: dawn, shine, of light and of Christ
senses.definition: Light breaking out of darkness, and Christ rising as that light.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “to those sitting in the land and shadow of death light has dawned (דְּנַח)”, quoting Isa 9:1.
Peshitta: God who said “light shall shine (נֶדְנַח) out of darkness” has shone (דְּנַח) in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
Peshitta: the god of this age blinded them, “that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ should not dawn (נֶדְנַח) on them”.
Peshitta: נֶדְנַח for ἀνατείλῃ, the morning star rising in your hearts until the day dawns.
Peshitta: “our Lord has risen (דְּנַח) from Judah”.

senses.definition: God causing his sun to rise.

evidence.note: Peshitta: the Father “makes his sun rise (דְּמַדְנַח) on the good and on the evil”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s word for the east, the counterpart of מִזְרָח, rendering ἀνατολή.

senses.definition: The quarter where the sun rises, and as with מִזְרָח, with the west the whole earth.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “many will come from the east (מַדְנְחָא) and from the west”.
Peshitta: the lightning comes out from the east and is seen to the west.
Peshitta: wise men came from the east to Jerusalem.
Peshitta: “we have seen his star in the east”.
Peshitta: an angel ascending “from the rising (מַדְנְחַי) of the sun”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s noun for the dawn, used once in the New Testament, of Christ’s coming in Zechariah’s song.

senses.definition: The rising of light, said of the Christ whom God sends to shine on those in darkness.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “by which the dawning (דֶּנְחָא) from on high visits us”, “to give light to those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death” (Luk 1:79), as Yahweh’s glory rises on Zion in Isa 60:1–3.

cognates.gloss: shine, be bright; (of the sun) rise
cognates.note: The Targum renders Gen 32:32 “the sun rose” with it, and rabbinic Aramaic says of the sun שִׁמְשָׁא דַּנְחָא “the sun shines”. Aramaic d answers Hebrew ז where the older sound is ḏ, as in דְּהַב against זָהָב; the n for r is a change within Aramaic.

evidence.locator: D00926, דְּנַח, “to shine, be bright”; Targ. Gen. 32:32
root 463 DNK (ܕܢܚ), lexeme 734 DNK “rise, shine, dawn; (aphel) make rise”, lexeme 735 DNKA “dawn, dayspring”

cognates.note: The Targums’ word for the east, formed as מִזְרָח is, with a place prefix מ on the verb “rise”: Targ. Num 34:11 and Targ. Job 1:3, where it stands for Hebrew קֶדֶם.

evidence.locator: M00296, מָדִינְחָא (מְדִנְחָא), “East”; constr. מַדְנַח, Targ. Num. 34:11

cognates.note: The only use of Arabic ḏrḥ near the sense of light: a colour word, perhaps of the red of dawn, but Lane gives nothing of rising or shining, and the root’s other words (ḏaraḥa “winnow”, ḏurrāḥ “cantharis, the Spanish fly”) are far from it. The consonants are what the Aramaic leads one to expect (ḏ, and ḥ).

doctrine.statement: In the prophets the rising of light is Yahweh’s coming to his people: his glory “has risen upon you”, “upon you Yahweh will rise”, while darkness covers the earth, and nations and kings come to the brightness of Zion’s rising (Isa 60:1–3); to those who fear his name “the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its wings” (Mal 3:20). Zechariah, at John’s birth, speaks of the “dawning from on high” (ἀνατολή; Peshitta דֶּנְחָא) that visits us “to shine on those sitting in darkness” (Luk 1:78–79); Matthew says the light “has risen” on Galilee when Jesus began to preach there (Mat 4:16); Hebrews, that “our Lord has risen out of Judah” (Heb 7:14); Paul, that the God who said “light shall shine out of darkness” has shone in our hearts “to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2Co 4:6). From the verses: the light that rises is Yahweh’s glory, and it has risen in his Son, in whose face that glory is seen; the rest of Isa 60, the nations walking in Zion’s light, waits for its fulfilment.

The law sets the native (אֶזְרָח) and the sojourner side by side: “one law for the native and for the sojourner” (Exo 12:49; Num 15:29); a sojourner who is circumcised may keep the Passover and “will be like the native of the land” (Exo 12:48); Israel is to love the sojourner as the native, “for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt” (Lev 19:34); and the native is to dwell in booths for seven days to remember that Yahweh made Israel dwell in booths when he brought them out (Lev 23:42–43). In the land as Ezekiel sees it divided, sojourners who have settled among Israel inherit “as the native among the sons of Israel” (Ezk 47:22). Paul tells Gentile believers that they were once “strangers from the covenants of promise”, but are “no longer strangers and sojourners but fellow citizens with the saints” (Eph 2:12, 19), and that those who are Christ’s are Abraham’s seed and heirs (Gal 3:29). From the verses: belonging in Israel was never birth alone; the stranger who took on the covenant was counted with the native, and in Christ the Gentile is made a citizen of Israel’s hope.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 and Numbers 10 (אֶזְרָח, Lev 23:42). Root key זרח as the database keys it. Proper names and gentilics left out of the words and given no name entry (the task named none): זֶרַח Zerah (g.cj.ac; Judah’s son, Gen 38:30, named because he “rose” or broke out; also an Edomite, a Simeonite, a Levite and the Cushite of 2Ch 14:8), זַרְחִי Zerahite (g.cj.ad), זְרַחְיָה Zerahiah (g.cj.ae), אֶזְרָחִי Ezrahite (g.cj.ag; Ethan and Heman, who are sons of Zerah in 1Ch 2:6, so a gentilic of Zerah, not of אֶזְרָח), יִזְרַחְיָה Izrahiah (g.cj.ai) and יִזְרָח Izrahite (g.cj.ah). Zero-token cross-references a.ci.ad, j.bd.ad and m.bj.ae are left out. g.cj.aa counts two tokens of the name Zerah (Gen 38:30; 1Ch 2:4) and shares Psa 112:4 with g.cj.ac. Peshitta: SEDRA root 463 DNK, lexemes 734–736, located in the BFBS word list (Mat 2:1, 2, 9; 4:16; 5:45; 8:11; 13:6; 24:27; Mrk 4:6; 16:2; Luk 1:78; 12:54; 13:29; 2Co 4:4, 6; Heb 7:14; Jas 1:11; 2Pe 1:19; Rev 7:2; 16:12; 21:13); the Peshitta wording was not read verse by verse in a rendered text, so the quoted Syriac forms rest on SEDRA’s vocalised word list. Payne Smith not consulted. No Ugaritic cognate in Segert’s glossary; Ge’ez (Dillmann, Leslau) and Akkadian beyond Oracc not consulted; the Oracc candidates (zarû “winnow”, zēru “seed”, zêru “hate”) are other roots. Wiktionary links Arabic شَرَقَ “rise (of the sun)” and شَرْق “east”, but its consonants š-r-q do not answer to z-r-ḥ, so it is left out. אֶזְרָח has no cognate sharing its sense, so the root’s cognates count against it; its tie to “rise” is open. The Septuagint renders it αὐτόχθων and ἐγχώριος, neither in the New Testament, so no Greek is given. Open questions: (1) whether אֶזְרָח belongs with זרח; (2) Isa 60:3 זֶרַח given its own word under g.cj.ab rather than folded into the verb; (3) the doctrine’s reading of Mal 3:20 through Luk 1:78.
